## Command Standard Operating Procedure
# Part one: Succession, and acting. Succession dictates who is granted the title of Acting Captain in an emergency, or otherwise simply lacking one. If a Command member is missing, dead, or declines acting, it goes to the next in line. If no one willingly steps up and there is an active emergency requiring acting, it must be voted on who must take the role out of all living and available members of Command. If any former command is in an NT-Design Cyborg chassis, they may vote but cannot be acting. Succession is as follows: Captain \> Head of Personnel \> Head of Security \> Chief Engineer \> Chief Medical Officer \> Research Director \> Quartermaster [textlink="(or Salvage)" link="SOPPSDepCargo"] \> NT Personnel [textlink="(see NTP SOP)" link="SOPPSDepNTP"] If there are no heads available (or alive) to take the role, the highest level of available Security should take it [textlink="(having the same succession as HoS, as outlined in Sec SoP)" link="SOPPSDepSecurity"] If there is no security (assigned and alive), and there are no members of Salvage, NT Personnel roles may take the title. This should be considered in an extreme emergency, as the station generally should govern itself.
# Part two: Command armaments
Captain (including Acting) is authorized to carry their Antique Laser Pistol and Disabler at all times. Upon discovery of a credible threat, the Captain may carry handcuffs to support their non-lethal protection. The Captain should carry either their assigned pinpointer or the Nuclear Authentication Disk (a.k.a. the NAD); it is highly advised the Captain carries the disk itself. The Captain may issue the pinpointer (or disk) to any mindshielded personnel they trust, though primarily Command. Additional pinpointers should be kept in the vault when possible, unless there is an explicit reason to provide it to someone else.
Other members of Command should not be carrying armaments (except a disabler) unless there is a confirmed, credible threat that endangers their life. Upon this discovery, the Deckard may be issued as necessary to a member of Command for self-defense, and handcuffs to support non-lethal self-defense (in addition to a disabler, if they were not assigned one already)
# Part three: Corruption At all times, Command is intended to set themselves as a great example to the rest of the station, due to this, (unless you are an Antagonist that was fairly promoted) Command should not act corrupt in any way. There are some exceptions, mainly for the (acting) Captain but other department heads too if it applies; if someone poses a greater threat to the entire station (or for a head, their entire department), bargaining is allowed. (This means gimmicks such as nuclear operatives buying the station, is allowed at player discretion. If your character wouldn't agree to the terms, you are not forced against your characters' judgement) For antagonists that were promoted to a Head role, you may act corrupt within reason to complete your objectives. Try to set a good example otherwise, especially as it will help you maintain your cover!
